sentenceSets.sentence: The remuneration for the role did not reflect the actual demands of the position, a discrepancy that had accumulated through a series of decisions no one had intended.

answerChoices.reasoning: Very close in this context, but this word often points to making someone whole for a loss or injury, while the sentence weighs what the job pays against what the job requires.
A salary is one fixed component, whereas the mismatch described accumulated across many decisions and would take in every form of payment attached to the role.
Too colloquial and narrow for a sentence about an institutional discrepancy built up over years of formal decisions.
A stipend is a fixed allowance, usually modest and for trainees or fellows, which sits awkwardly with a position described as having real and growing demands.
A reward is discretionary recognition for something achieved, not the standing terms attached to holding the position.
A budget is money the role controls, not money the role receives, so it could not be compared to the demands on its holder.
An allowance covers expenses, which would not be expected to track the difficulty of the work.
An honorarium is a token payment for an occasional service, at odds with an ongoing position whose demands grew over time.
The sentence measures the mismatch in something that accumulates through administrative decisions, not in reputation.
The demands of the position are the other side of the comparison, so the blank must be what is being weighed against them.
Nothing suggests the role carries a punishment; the discrepancy is about what the job offers its holder.

sentenceSets.sentence: She agreed to write the report without remuneration, expecting the contacts it brought her to be worth more than any fee.

answerChoices.reasoning: Plausible, but the sentence contrasts what she gave up with contacts gained in return, framing the missing item as what one earns for professional work rather than a transfer of money.
Recompense answers a loss or an injury, whereas she is doing commissioned work and forgoing what the work would ordinarily earn her.
Reimbursement returns money already spent, and the sentence mentions no expenses she incurred writing the report.
Wages are paid hourly to an employee, while she has agreed to a single piece of work on her own terms.
Profit is what remains after costs in a venture, not the sum she waived by writing a report for free.
Royalties depend on continuing sales or use, but the sentence weighs the contacts against a straightforward fee.
Funding underwrites a project's costs rather than rewarding the person who did the writing.
Credit is public acknowledgment, and the sentence already gives her a nonmonetary gain in the contacts she expected.
The sentence says she agreed, and the missing item is set against a fee in the same clause.
Working without grumbling is not what the comparison to a fee is measuring.
Oversight has nothing to do with a trade of income for professional connections.

sentenceSets.sentence: Shareholders demanded a full accounting of executive remuneration after the share price fell by half.

answerChoices.reasoning: Very close, though this word carries an archaic, chiefly legal flavor tied to holders of public office rather than to company executives answering to shareholders.
Bonuses are only the variable portion, but shareholders angry about a halved share price would want everything the executives received, not one line item.
Perquisites are the fringe benefits attached to a post, a narrow slice of what a full accounting after such a collapse would cover.
A payout is a one-time disbursement, while the demand described covers what the executives are paid for holding their jobs.
Turnover refers either to revenue or to staff departures, neither of which is what shareholders would demand an accounting of when the share price halves.
Expense claims are money spent on the company's behalf, not what the executives themselves take home.
Severance applies to executives who have left, and the sentence describes scrutiny of those still in post.
Incentives describe the design of a pay scheme rather than the total sums the executives received.
Turning up to meetings is not the grievance a halved share price would provoke among shareholders.
Length of service cannot be the subject of a financial accounting.
Manners have nothing to do with a demand for financial disclosure.
